column4: The Egyptian purchaser tells his wife to honor Joseph's lodging and considers taking him as a son; this is a direct non-biological household receiving and raising a child.
When Joseph reaches full strength, God gives him judgment and knowledge, a second child-to-maturity sequence alongside Moses' growth in 28:14.
When the promised son reaches the age to work with Abraham, father and son deliberate together; maturity appears as shared responsibility within a parent-child bond.
The ruling explicitly concerns orphan girls and weak children and commands justice for orphans, extending guardianship to those structurally least able to protect themselves.
Jesus declares himself devoted to his mother and not made arrogant or wretched, giving the child-side response to parental mercy a distinct formulation.
Moses' sister is told to follow him and keeps watch from a distance; her own act is sibling vigilance during the child's transfer between households.
After proportioning the human, God gives spirit, hearing, sight, and hearts; bodily formation opens into capacities for perception and learning.
This ayah identifies Moses' mother as the recipient of divine inspiration; 20:39 gives the instruction itself, while 20:38 supplies its maternal beginning.
Jacob warns his son Joseph not to disclose the vision to his brothers, a father's specific effort to protect a child's vulnerable future within a divided household.
Joseph's Rabb will teach him interpretation and complete His favor upon him and Jacob's family, joining education, divine lordship, and a family-wide niʿma.
Abraham asks his Lord for a righteous child; the prayer makes offspring a hoped-for trust before the good news and later maturity in 37:101–102.
The answer is glad tidings of a forbearing boy, giving the desired child an ethically formed quality before the father-son scene of 37:102.
Noah calls his son to board the ark and avoid the unbelievers; parental protection appears as an urgent invitation to safety.
Noah pleads that his son belongs to his family, making biological and household kinship the explicit ground of his appeal.
God gives His servant mercy and teaches him knowledge from Himself; the verse directly joins raḥma and instruction, the meeting the section develops through the teacher.
Fear of failing to deal justly with orphans is made a threshold for the marriage ruling; it keeps the weak dependent's right in view within household formation.
People are enjoined to goodness toward parents, while obedience has a boundary when they press toward association; it parallels the qualified filial kindness of 31:15.
Jesus is taught scripture and wisdom and speaks to people in the cradle and in maturity; teaching and a life-span of formation are held in one address.
The human is created from a mixed drop and given hearing and sight; physical origin is immediately linked to capacities through which learning and testing occur.
God creates the human from water and makes bonds of blood relation and marriage; it broadens the womb-derived kinship image to the family ties that make a household.
In the cattle passage, people have benefits and drinks from the animals; this repeats the domestic nourishment activated by the sheep-kept-for-milk detail.
Pharaoh's family picks Moses up only for him to become an enemy and grief to them; before 28:9 proposes adoption, this ayah makes the foster household a dangerous reversal.
Answering Noah's plea in 11:45, God says the son is not of his family because of unrighteous conduct; it marks a boundary where biological kinship alone does not secure the familial claim.
The boy's believing parents are feared to be burdened by his rebellion and disbelief, a hard case in which parent-child welfare is judged beyond ordinary visible care.
Following 18:80, the stated replacement is a child better in purity and nearer in mercy for the parents; its own contribution is the mercy-oriented outcome of that difficult boundary case.
